stem: A client wants a second opinion before a major elective operation. Which nursing response is most appropriate?

options.A: Discourage another opinion because it may damage the therapeutic relationship.
options.B: Tell the client that only the surgeon can decide whether another opinion may be sought.
options.C: Support the client's stated choice and help coordinate the records or referral process needed for another opinion.
options.D: Advise the client to have the operation first and seek another opinion afterward if concerns remain.

rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan places advocacy, client rights, and referrals within Management of Care. It directs nurses to discuss identified treatment options and respect client decisions, act as client advocates, advocate for client rights and needs, assess the need for referrals, and identify documents needed when referring a client. Therefore C is the most appropriate response. A discourages the client's informed choice, B incorrectly makes another clinician the gatekeeper for the client's decision to seek additional information, and D defeats the purpose of obtaining another opinion before an elective treatment decision.
educational_objective: Support a client's decision to seek additional information before elective treatment by advocating for the client's choice and facilitating appropriate referral and record coordination.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Management of Care, printed pp.20-22: Advocacy — discuss identified treatment options with client and respect their decisions; act in role of client advocate; Client Rights — discuss treatment options/decisions and advocate for client rights and needs; Referrals — assess need for referrals, obtain necessary orders as applicable, and identify documents to include when referring a client such as the medical record/referral form.
source_claim_supported: Nursing advocacy includes respecting client treatment decisions and facilitating appropriate referral/record processes when the client seeks additional information before an elective treatment decision.

source_original.stem: A client wants a second opinion before a major elective operation. Which nursing response is most appropriate?

options.A: Discourage another opinion because it may damage the therapeutic relationship.
options.B: Tell the client that only the surgeon can decide whether a second opinion is allowed.
options.C: Support the client's choice and help identify how records or referrals can be obtained.
options.D: Advise the client to have the operation first and seek another opinion afterward.

source_original.rationale: Supporting an informed client choice and helping coordinate information or referral is consistent with nursing advocacy and client rights. Option C is correct. A and B undermine autonomy, and D defeats the purpose of seeking another opinion before an elective decision.
source_original.source_detail: Management of Care — Advocacy/Client Rights activity statements: advocate for client rights and preferences, provide information needed for informed decisions, facilitate referrals/continuity, and collaborate with the care team. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, assignment/delegation, advocacy/client rights, continuity/referral, legal scope, professional limitations and emergency/quality-management activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the advocacy/referral construct and key C. Tightened the wording so the item supports the client's stated choice and referral/record coordination without asserting a universal legal entitlement to a second opinion that would require separate jurisdiction-specific legal sourcing.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Client advocacy and referral for additional treatment opinion
audit_findings.source_authority: Current official NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: Management of Care > Advocacy, Client Rights, and Referrals, printed pp.20-22
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item is limited to NCSBN-supported advocacy, respect for treatment decisions, referral assessment, and record/referral coordination. It does not make an unsourced jurisdiction-specific legal claim about a statutory right to second opinion.

distractor_audit.A: Undermines advocacy and respect for the client's treatment decision process.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrectly makes the surgeon the gatekeeper for the client's choice to seek additional information.
distractor_audit.C: Correct and directly aligned with advocacy/referral content.
distractor_audit.D: Defeats the purpose of obtaining additional information before an elective treatment decision.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C supports the client's stated decision and facilitates the referral/information process without overstepping nursing scope.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are nurse responses to the same request; no legalistic or length cue identifies the answer.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care — Advocacy, Client Rights, and Referrals.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-audited the NCSBN PDF text and rendered Management of Care pages, all alternatives, rationale, objective, legal-claim boundary, ambiguity and cueing. C remained uniquely defensible with no unsupported legal precision.
